title: More of Duke's late cruelties: Norris Turney and Tony Watkins
summary: Willard tells how Duke doubled the tempo behind Norris Turney until he quit and left Tony Watkins waiting in the wings of a television show; Bigard agrees he got terrible.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, he did a lot of strange things, like he got Norris Turney to quit by doubling the tempo behind him on his solos. Now, you say he played too slowly for you.

He played so fast as to try to, I guess, make it too fast for Norris to be able to play, and I was told by members of the band that Norris, right in the middle of his own number, closed up his instruments in their cases and walked off the stand, and that was when he quit because he was doing it to him.

And that was, you know, in later years. And several of the people -- he would tell the singers, whoever they were, in the band, and one time he told Tony Watkins that he should call home and tell his relatives in Philadelphia that he would be on, I think it was the Merv Griffin show -- some television show Duke was doing. And Tony should be sure and wear his tuxedo to the television station because Duke wanted to really put on a nice performance.
So Tony did. He alerted all his relatives. And then he was kept standing in the wings, like you say Ray Nance was. Duke never even acknowledged the fact that he was there and he was never on.
